To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an HSV2 DNA binding protein is expressed in 38 percent of human cervical carcinomas and severe dysplasia.
an HSV2 antigen was detected in 38% (11/29) of cervical cancers, and in 4% (1/25) of cervical dysplasias.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HSV2 in human cervical cancer, and with the possible mechanism of HSV2-mediated transformation of human cells in vitro and in vivo.
the development of a vaccine to prevent the development of cervical cancer.
the role of HSV2 in the development of human cervical carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSV2 is a factor in the aetiology of human cervical cancer.
the evidence for the involvement of HSV2 in human cervical cancer is still circumstantial and indirect, but it is now more compelling.
the association of HSV2 with human cervical cancer remains to be established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSV2 is associated with cervical cancer and is not associated with benign cervical lesions.
